title: Exercise 7A · Q12
summary: Find KB in ΔHBK, then CB, then AB in ΔABC, and finally AH = AB − HB.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q12: In ΔABC, AC = 43 cm and ∠B = 90°. H lies on AB such that HB = 15 cm and K lies on CB such that CK = 19 cm. Given that HK = 22 cm, find the length of AH.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In **ΔABC**, **AC = 43 cm** and **∠B = 90°**. **H** lies on **AB** such that **HB = 15 cm** and **K** lies on **CB** such that **CK = 19 cm**. Given that **HK = 22 cm**, we have to find **AH**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔHBK, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **HK**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. (∠HBK is the same angle as ∠ABC.) **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{HK^2} &= \role{legA}{HB^2} + \role{legB}{KB^2} \\ \role{legB}{KB^2} &= \role{hyp}{HK^2} - \role{legA}{HB^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{HK^2} &= \role{legA}{HB^2} + \role{legB}{KB^2} \\ \role{legB}{KB^2} &= \role{hyp}{HK^2} - \role{legA}{HB^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{22^2} - \role{legA}{15^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{484} - \role{legA}{225} \\ &= \role{legB}{259}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 259 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{HK^2} &= \role{legA}{HB^2} + \role{legB}{KB^2} \\ \role{legB}{KB^2} &= \role{hyp}{HK^2} - \role{legA}{HB^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{22^2} - \role{legA}{15^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{484} - \role{legA}{225} \\ &= \role{legB}{259} \\ \role{legB}{KB} &= \sqrt{259} = 16.09\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find CB
steps.narration: **CB** is made of **CK** and **KB**.\[\begin{aligned}CB &= CK + KB \\ &= 19 + 16.09 \\ &= 35.09\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AB^2} \\ \role{legB}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legA}{CB^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AB^2} \\ \role{legB}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legA}{CB^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{43^2} - \role{legA}{35.09^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1849} - \role{legA}{1231.31} \\ &= \role{legB}{617.69}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 617.69 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{CB^2} + \role{legB}{AB^2} \\ \role{legB}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legA}{CB^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{43^2} - \role{legA}{35.09^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1849} - \role{legA}{1231.31} \\ &= \role{legB}{617.69} \\ \role{legB}{AB} &= \sqrt{617.69} = 24.85\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find AH
steps.narration: **AH** is what is left of **AB** after taking away **HB**.\[\begin{aligned}AH &= AB - HB \\ &= 24.85 - 15 \\ &= \role{ans}{9.85\ \text{cm}}\ \text{(3 s.f.)}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Right angle?

options.label: Yes — it is the same angle as ∠ABC
No — H is not a vertex

challenges.hint: H lies on AB and K lies on CB.
challenges.explain: H is on AB and K is on CB, so ∠HBK is ∠ABC, which is 90°.

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
